about: The assistant's fixed dialog. No model: every line is a template, every chip is an intent id from registry.json. Runtime copy: frontend/lib/workspace/dialog.json (identical; a test asserts it). The 'examples' table is the test table for lib/workspace/dialog.ts.

grammar.template: Replace {name} with String(context[name]) or, when context has no such key, the derived value of that name. A name with neither throws Error('dialog: missing {name}'). No other syntax.
grammar.when: An object; every key must hold. A key holds when: its value is a literal and context[key] === literal; or its value is {"gt": n} and typeof context[key] === 'number' and context[key] > n; or its value is {"present": true} and context[key] is a non-empty string; or {"present": false} and it is not. A missing key never holds, except {"present": false}. An empty object always holds.
grammar.tab: For overview.attention the context's 'tab' is the effective tab: the requested tab, except that when the requested tab holds no services and the other tab does, the other tab (so the reply and the screen agree).
grammar.variants: The first variant whose 'when' holds supplies the reply. The last variant of every turn has an empty 'when'.
grammar.chips: A chip is shown only when its 'when' holds (no 'when' means always). Chips keep their order. 'params' are merged into the target intent's URL parameters. The renderer returns every chip whose 'when' holds; the thread hook then drops a chip whose target intent is not offered to this session (registry canOpen, which includes the phase), so a chip never points at a screen that does not exist.
grammar.echo: renderTurn(intentId, context, { withEcho }) computes the echo only when withEcho is true, and returns echo null otherwise. The thread hook passes withEcho true only when the turn is added after another turn in the same page visit, so a reload never needs an echo's placeholders.
